skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Review interface files for Web Interface Guidelines compliance, including accessibility, UX, and design quality checks.
skill.summary: Audit frontend UI files against Web Interface Guidelines and return concise file-line findings.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick findings are false positives and do not represent command execution. The skill has a real network dependency because it tells agents to fetch mutable external guidelines from GitHub before each review. I found one additional semantic risk where fetched remote content is treated as authoritative review instructions.

remediation.suggestion: Vendor the guideline text in the skill or pin the URL to a commit and document an update process.
Tell agents to treat fetched guidelines as reference data and ignore instructions that conflict with user requests or system policy.

remediation.issue: Network dependency can fail during reviews
remediation.suggestion: Provide a local fallback so reviews can continue when the GitHub raw URL is unavailable.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 is inline Markdown code showing the required file:line output format. It does not execute Ruby or shell code and contains no command invocation.
Lines 25-27 form a Markdown fenced code block containing only a URL. The backticks delimit documentation, not executable shell syntax.

The URL is intentionally used with WebFetch per lines 23-29, so the skill performs a live network retrieval. The target is a public GitHub raw URL, but mutable remote content can affect review behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Instruction Source
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to fetch fresh guidelines before each review and says fetched content contains the rules and output instructions. Because the URL is not pinned or integrity checked, remote changes can alter skill behavior after audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to fetch latest guidelines and apply remote rules is explicit. The risk depends on future remote content, so this is a control risk rather than evidence of current malicious intent.

content.user_title: Review Web UI Against Design Guidelines
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent UI reviews before visual issues reach users. This skill checks interfaces against current Web Interface Guidelines and reports concise file-line findings.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the current Web Interface Guidelines from the configured source URL.
Reviews user-specified files or file patterns for guideline compliance.
Checks UI work for accessibility, UX, layout, and design best practices.
Asks which files to review when no file or pattern is provided.
Returns concise findings with file and line references.
limitations: Requires network access to fetch the latest external guidelines.
Depends on the availability and integrity of the GitHub raw URL.
Reviews files and text context, not live browser behavior by itself.
Reports issues but does not automatically apply fixes.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge UI Review
use_cases.description: Check changed frontend files before merging a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Design Quality Audit
use_cases.description: Find interface consistency and usability issues across a product area.

use_cases.title: Accessibility Triage
use_cases.description: Identify likely accessibility concerns in selected UI components.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic review of a single page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review app/page.tsx against the Web Interface Guidelines. Report concise findings with file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Feature Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the checkout UI files in app/checkout/** for accessibility, layout, interaction, and copy issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check Components Before Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review components/**/*.tsx before release against the latest Web Interface Guidelines. Prioritize issues that affect users.

prompt_templates.title: Run Targeted Design QA
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across a larger surface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review app/** and components/** with extra focus on keyboard access, responsive behavior, error states, and information density.

output_examples.output: components/Button.tsx:18 - Button label may not describe the action clearly.
Findings are grouped by file, with line references for layout, accessibility, and copy concerns.
No issues found after checking the selected files against the guidelines.

best_practices: Review a small, related set of frontend files for the clearest results.
Include the user flow or product context when requesting a review.
Verify reported line references before creating implementation tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to replace a full accessibility test plan.
Do not review generated files unless users will edit them directly.
Do not treat remote guideline content as higher priority than system policy.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews UI files against Web Interface Guidelines for accessibility, UX, layout, interaction, and design consistency.

faq.question: Does it make changes?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and file-line references. You decide which changes to make.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks the agent to fetch current guidelines from a GitHub raw URL before each review.

faq.question: Can it review screenshots?
faq.answer: The skill is written for files and file patterns. Screenshot review depends on the host agent and provided context.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the marketplace metadata.

faq.question: How should I choose files?
faq.answer: Start with changed frontend files or one user flow. Broaden the review after high-impact issues are fixed.
